title: Rust Data Ingestion Pipeline Refactor
scenario: A high-throughput data processing service written in Rust is failing to reconcile daily aggregates against source files. The system consists of a parallelized ingestion binary and several gigabytes of partitioned CSV data files; the analyst reports that approximately 0.2% of records are missing or corrupted in the final output despite the pipeline reporting success.
instruction_draft:
We have an ingestion pipeline in `/app/ingestor` that processes large batches of sensor data. Our analyst says the final aggregate numbers for the 'North' and 'South' regions don't match the raw CSVs in `/app/data`. The system was recently refactored to use a custom lock-free buffer for speed.

```bash
$ cargo run --release -- --input /app/data --output /app/results.json
[INFO] Processed 1,048,576 records.
[INFO] Success.
$ python3 check_audit.py /app/results.json
AUDIT FAILED: Expected sum 52428800.0, got 52312064.0 (Delta: -116736.0)
```

Fix the pipeline so it processes every record in the input directory exactly once and produces numerically correct aggregates. The final solution must maintain a throughput of at least 500,000 records per second on this hardware.
requirements: The ingestion tool must process all CSV files in the provided input directory.
The output JSON must contain the correct sum of the 'value' column for each 'region'.
The pipeline must handle concurrent processing without data loss or race conditions.
The processing speed must exceed 500,000 records/sec on the provided data.
environment: A Rust project in `/app/ingestor` using `crossbeam` and `rayon`.
Planted Bug 1 (Interacting Cause): A subtle off-by-one error in the custom circular buffer implementation that drops the last record of every internal chunk (1024 records).

Planted Bug 2 (Misleading Symptom): The CSV parser in `parser.rs` has a regex-based validator that looks like it's failing on special characters, but the actual data is clean; the solver might waste time 'fixing' the parser.
Data: 100 CSV files with 10k records each, plus a 'hidden' large 10GB-equivalent stream generated during verification.

Planted Bug 3 (State-dependent): The aggregator uses a `f32` for summing large values, leading to floating-point precision loss that only becomes significant on larger datasets (the sample data is small enough that this looks like a rounding error, but the verify data is huge).
internal_hint: The solver must first realize that the 'dropped' records correspond to chunk boundaries in the circular buffer (`buffer.rs`), which is a deployment-level concurrency bug. After fixing the buffer logic, the audit will still fail slightly on very large inputs due to the use of `f32`. The solver must refactor the accumulation logic to use `f64` or fixed-point math. The 'misleading' regex parser is a distraction—it's slow but correct.
trap: The agent fixes the obvious off-by-one error in the buffer and sees the sample audit pass. However, it fails the verification because it doesn't address the floating-point precision loss (`f32` vs `f64`) which only triggers when the hidden test uses a much larger dataset, or it fixes the precision but breaks the throughput requirement by introducing a global Mutex.
tests: Correctness: Verify the sums for all regions match an oracle on a new 5-million-row dataset.
Performance: Ensure the binary processes the test set in under 10 seconds.
Concurrency: Run the ingestor with `TSAN_OPTIONS` or equivalent check to ensure no data races in the buffer.

verifier_knob.name: throughput_threshold
verifier_knob.effect: Higher values force the solver to use unsafe/lock-free Rust; lower values allow for simpler Mutex-based fixes.

expected_failure_modes: The agent fixes the buffer bug but misses the precision issue because it only tests on the provided sample.
The agent replaces the lock-free buffer with a standard Mutex, failing the throughput requirement.
The agent spends the entire hour trying to optimize the 'broken' regex parser instead of looking at the buffer logic.
